A1.justification: Both PDFs present the same StreamMind study, and all 13 pages are readable and comparable, including equations, nine tables and seven figures. Neither supplied PDF contains a separate appendix, although Sections 2.3 and 2.5 reference one.

before.justification: v1 reports original streaming and offline benchmark results, inference-efficiency measurements, perception visualizations and ablations in Sections 3–5.

after.justification: v3 retains these original benchmark results, efficiency measurements, visualizations and ablations.

M1.justification: The EPFE, Cognition Gate, shallow-layer transfer, perception-memory sampling, two-stage training and weighted loss remain unchanged in Section 2 and Algorithm 1.

E1.justification: Both retain Ego4D and SoccerNet-Caption streaming evaluation, COIN recognition and forecasting tasks, and Ego4D LTA. No dataset, task, domain or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged throughout the experiments. Tables 1–2 retain VideoLLM-Online and VideoLLM-MoD, with LION-FS remaining an Ego4D-only comparison using paper-reported results; offline and ablation comparators also match.

E3.justification: Both report the same 2-FPS training input, one epoch per stage, learning rates, metrics and hardware settings. The efficiency evaluation still tests 5–100-FPS inputs on A100 and H100 GPUs.

E4.justification: The EPFE-versus-STC visualization, silence/response weighting analysis, gate architecture/initialization/depth ablations, feature-extractor comparison and football demonstration are unchanged in Sections 4, 5 and 7.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests or error bars for the reported experiments. No uncertainty-reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: All result entries and plotted findings match. For example, Table 1 retains StreamMind TriggerAcc values of 43.34% on Ego4D and 52.18% on SoccerNet; offline scores, efficiency curves and ablation results are also unchanged.

T1.justification: The streaming-dialogue formulation, state-space update, complexity arguments and empirical balancing-weight relation remain unchanged, including Equations 1–5. No formal assumption, derivation or proof is added or revised.

C1.justification: Both retain the same claims about event-gated cognition, processing up to 100 FPS on one A100 and state-of-the-art performance. Changing the abstract's application example from 'Game AI Copilot' to 'Game AI' does not materially alter the scientific claims.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning EPFE event memory, shallow-layer gating and dataset-dependent silence/response weighting are identical. No substantive limitation, failure condition or applicability qualification is added or revised.

D1.justification: v3 adds an abstract statement that code and data are available, together with a project link absent from v1. Implementation details otherwise remain unchanged. The PDFs establish the added access information but cannot verify the linked resources.

R1.justification: Section 6, the discussion of prior methods and all 76 references remain unchanged. The positioning of event-gated invocation relative to earlier streaming-video approaches is retained.

P1.justification: First-page edits revise affiliations, replace email and corresponding-author footnotes with an internship note, shorten 'Game AI Copilot' to 'Game AI', and add the resource-access sentence. The scientific prose and section organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The revised affiliation block, longer abstract and replacement footnote produce minor first-page reflow. All seven figures and nine tables retain their content, captions, structure and placement.

improvement.justification: The new code-and-data pointer modestly improves reproducibility guidance by providing access information absent from v1. Methods, evidence and conclusions remain unchanged, so the benefit is limited to documentation; the PDFs do not establish whether the linked resources are functional or complete.
